passages.title: The Recipe for Four
paragraphs: Our family recipe made pancakes for four people, but six cousins were coming for lunch. With Mum and me, there would be eight of us. I needed twice as much of each ingredient（原料）. I wrote the new amounts beside the old ones and measured everything carefully. Mum heated the pan while I mixed the batter（面糊）. The first pancake was rather thick, so we added a little milk. Soon, a warm pile waited on the table. Everyone helped themselves to pancakes. My maths homework had never smelled so delicious before.

passages.title: A Seat beside the Stage
paragraphs: At the school concert, my job was to help visitors find their seats. One guest used a wheelchair（轮椅）. I nearly pointed her towards a narrow row before noticing the space beside the stage. I asked whether she would prefer to sit there with her family. She smiled and said yes. I checked that the path was clear and showed them the way. Later, our teacher thanked us for welcoming everyone. I learned that good service（服务） begins with paying attention to people and asking about their needs（需要）, rather than guessing.

passages.title: The Puppet behind the Curtain
paragraphs: For our class play, I worked a small fox puppet（木偶） from behind a curtain（幕布）. At first, I moved it whenever I spoke. Then our teacher suggested keeping it still while another character was talking. Suddenly, the fox seemed to be listening. I practised turning its head slowly and making it jump at the right moment. On the day of the show, nobody could see me, but the audience laughed at the fox. I felt proud of a performance made with my voice, my hands and a little imagination（想象力）.

passages.title: A Better Way to Queue
paragraphs: After art class, everyone rushed towards the same sink. Some pupils waited a long time, while others squeezed past them. We needed a fairer system（办法）. The next lesson, each table took a turn, and the rest of us cleared away paper while waiting. Nobody had to stand in a crowded（拥挤的） line. We finished cleaning at almost the same time. Our teacher asked which part had helped most. It was having another useful job to do. Waiting for something became easier when we could still make progress with our work.

passages.title: My Cousin’s Different Clock
paragraphs: My cousin moved to another country, and I wanted to call him after dinner. Mum checked the time there first. While we were getting ready for bed, he was still at school. Places around the world do not all share the same clock time. We chose a weekend hour that suited（适合） both families and marked it on our calendars（日历）. When his face appeared on the screen, sunlight filled his room. Outside my window, it was dark. We were talking at the same time, yet our days looked wonderfully different.

passages.title: The Second-Hand Puzzle
paragraphs: I bought a second-hand（二手的） puzzle at a small shop. The picture showed a busy harbour（港口） with boats and tall buildings. At home, I sorted the edge pieces first and worked slowly towards the middle. Near the end, I discovered that one piece was missing. I felt disappointed until my sister brought some card and coloured pencils. We drew the missing part and cut it carefully. It did not match perfectly, but it fitted into the space. Now our puzzle includes a tiny boat that belongs only to us.

passages.title: A Question for the Author
paragraphs: A children’s writer visited our school. I planned to ask how many books she had written, but someone asked that before my turn. While listening, I heard her mention a notebook beside her bed. I asked what she kept in it. She showed us a page of strange dreams, funny names and unfinished ideas. “Most will never become stories,” she said, “but I keep them anyway.” Her answer made me curious（好奇的） about my own small thoughts. That evening, I jotted down an idea before it could disappear（消失）.

passages.title: The Day I Was the Customer
paragraphs: Our classroom became a pretend shop during English class. I wanted to buy a blue notebook, but the shopkeeper offered a green one. I repeated my request more loudly. That did not help. Then I pointed to the blue cover and described its colour politely. My partner understood and handed it over. After we exchanged（交换） roles, I realised how hard it was to listen while counting coins. A useful conversation（对话） needs more than a loud voice. Clear words, patience and a chance to ask for help made our shop work.

passages.title: An Invitation with Missing Details
paragraphs: I made invitations for a Saturday drawing afternoon and handed them to my friends. They looked cheerful, with coloured pencils around the edges. Soon, questions arrived. “Which Saturday?” asked one friend. “Where shall we meet?” asked another. I had included the activity but forgotten the details（细节） people needed to attend. I made a second version（版本） with the date, time and place. Before sending it, I asked my brother to check it. A message is only useful when the reader can work out what to do next.

passages.title: The Compass in the Playground
paragraphs: Our teacher brought a compass outside and placed it flat on a wooden bench. After a little movement, its needle settled in one direction. We turned the compass, but the needle pointed back towards north. A compass helps us find directions（方向） because its magnetic（有磁性的） needle responds to Earth’s magnetic field. We marked north on a playground plan and added the other directions. Then we described where the school gate stood. I could finally tell the difference between knowing a place and explaining its position（位置） to someone else.

passages.title: The Spoon in the Glass
paragraphs: I put a spoon in a glass of water and looked at it from the side. It seemed bent where it entered the water. When I lifted it out, it was straight again. Our teacher explained that light changes direction as it passes between water and air. This makes the underwater part appear in a slightly different position（位置）. Nothing had happened to the spoon itself. I tried looking from several angles（角度）. What we see can depend on the path that light takes before it reaches our eyes.

passages.title: Why an Echo Answers
paragraphs: During a visit to a large, empty hall, I clapped once and heard a weaker clap follow. It sounded as if someone were answering. The guide said it was an echo（回声）. Sound had travelled to a distant（远处的） hard surface and bounced back. If the surface is far enough away, we hear the returning sound separately. Later, thick curtains were drawn across one wall, and the room sounded less lively. Soft materials take in some sound. I paid attention to my footsteps as we left the suddenly quieter space.

passages.title: The Tiny Drops on the Bottle
paragraphs: I took a cold bottle from the fridge and left it on the table. Soon, tiny drops appeared on the outside. I thought the bottle was leaking, but its lid was tight. Dad explained that water vapour（蒸气） in the air had cooled against the cold surface and changed into liquid. The drops came from the air around the bottle. I wiped it dry and watched more drops form. Even when something seems to come out of nowhere, there may be an explanation（解释） waiting to be discovered（发现）.

passages.title: A Magnet and a Box of Things
paragraphs: Our teacher gave us a magnet and a box containing paper clips, wooden blocks and plastic buttons. Before testing them, we wrote down our predictions（预测）. I thought the magnet would pick up every metal object. It attracted（吸引） the steel clips, but not a piece of aluminium（铝） foil. The teacher explained that only some materials are strongly attracted to an ordinary magnet. We sorted the objects according to our results. My first idea had been too simple. Trying things out helped me replace a guess with a clearer understanding（理解）.

passages.title: How a Feather Floats
paragraphs: A feather landed beside my shoe as I walked through the park. I watched it lift again in a gentle wind and turn slowly before settling. Later, I dropped a flat sheet of paper and a crumpled（揉皱的） one from the same height. The flat sheet fell more slowly. Its broad shape met more air as it moved down. A feather’s light weight and shape also help it drift（飘动）. I did not need to pick up the feather to enjoy the question it had brought into my afternoon.

passages.title: The Roots above the Path
paragraphs: On a woodland walk, we noticed tree roots crossing a narrow path. Our guide asked us to step carefully over them. Some roots grow close to the surface, spreading out to take in water and hold the tree in place. They do not all point straight down. I looked from the wide branches to the ground beneath them. There was another large part of the tree that I usually forgot. We stayed on the path and walked slowly, taking care not to damage（损坏） the exposed（露出的） roots.

passages.title: At the Fire Station
paragraphs: Our class visited a fire station on a quiet morning. A firefighter showed us the heavy clothes worn during emergencies（紧急情况）. We saw neatly arranged equipment（装备） and learned why everything had its own place. When a call comes, there may be little time to search. I tried lifting an empty hose and was surprised by its weight. Before we left, an alarm sounded, and the team moved quickly towards the engine. We stood back with our teacher. The visit ended suddenly, but their important work was just beginning.

passages.title: The Ferry across the River
paragraphs: I usually crossed the river through a tunnel, but on Sunday we took a ferry. We waited until the boat was ready and walked aboard with the other passengers. As it pulled away, the buildings seemed to slide along the water. A worker checked that everyone stayed behind the rail. The journey was short, yet I noticed cranes, smaller boats and wide patches of reflected sky. On the other bank, we waited our turn to leave. Taking a different route（路线） helped me look at my familiar city from another angle（角度）.

passages.title: The Secret of the Train Numbers
paragraphs: At the railway station, two trains were going to the same city within ten minutes of each other. I thought we could board either one. Dad showed me our ticket and pointed to the train number. Each service had its own number, departure time and platform. We followed the matching information on the large screen. Once aboard, we found our carriage and seats. The station seemed less confusing when I knew what to look for. A few small details（细节） connected our ticket to the right journey（行程）.

passages.title: The Garden on the Roof
paragraphs: Our neighbour showed us a garden on the roof of her building. The paths ran between raised beds filled with flowers and vegetables. She explained that the roof had been specially prepared to hold the extra weight and let water drain away. It was not simply soil poured onto concrete. We stayed in the visiting area and watched butterflies near the flowers. Above the busy street, the air felt quieter. A carefully planned space had made room for plants where I had expected only a bare surface（表面） of concrete（混凝土）.

passages.title: The Longest Ribbon
paragraphs: Three mice prepared ribbons for a party. Each wanted to bring the longest one. The first stretched his ribbon across a table. The second laid hers around a chair. The third curled hers into a pile. They argued because the shapes looked so different. An old mouse suggested laying all three straight, starting at the same line. At once, the answer became clear. The mice laughed and tied their ribbons together for a decoration（装饰物）. A fair comparison（比较） began when they agreed on how to measure the same thing.

passages.title: The Owl Who Asked Twice
paragraphs: An owl asked a rabbit to bring some leaves for his nest. The rabbit returned with fresh green ones, but the owl wanted dry leaves. “You should have known,” said the owl. The rabbit looked puzzled（困惑的）. The next morning, the owl asked again. This time, he explained what kind he needed and why. The rabbit brought exactly the right leaves. As they lined the nest, the owl apologised（道歉）. He had expected his friend to read his mind. Learning to make himself clear was part of becoming a better neighbour.

passages.title: The Missing Sound in the Song
paragraphs: Our class recorded a song for the school website. When we played it back, one voice was much louder than the others: mine. I had stood very close to the microphone（麦克风）. I wanted my grandparents to hear me clearly, but now they could hardly hear the class. We recorded the song again, with everyone standing at a similar distance. This time, I listened as well as sang. Our voices blended（融合） into a warmer sound. Being part of a group sometimes means leaving enough space for others to be heard.

passages.title: The Name on the Drawing
paragraphs: My friend and I made a drawing for a class display. She planned the picture, and I added most of the colour. When the teacher asked who had made it, I said my name first and stopped. My friend looked down at her desk. I quickly added, “We made it together.” Later, I wrote both names beneath the drawing. I had enjoyed the praise so much that I nearly forgot her work. Sharing credit（功劳） matters. A finished picture can belong to more than one artist（创作者）.

passages.title: A Sandwich for Someone Else
paragraphs: On our picnic morning, I offered to make my sister’s sandwich. I reached for tomato because it was my favourite filling. Then I remembered that she preferred cucumber. I asked what else she wanted and packed her lunch separately from mine. At the park, she opened it and smiled. “You remembered,” she said. I had almost made the easiest choice for myself instead of the right one for her. Doing someone a favour feels different when we consider their preferences（喜好）. Her happy lunch was worth a little extra effort（用心）.

passages.title: The Extra Point
paragraphs: During a classroom quiz, the teacher gave our team a point for an answer we had not finished. Nobody else seemed to notice. That point put us ahead. I whispered to my teammates, and we decided to raise our hands. The teacher thanked us and changed the score. Another team won in the end. I felt disappointed for a moment, but our answer sheet now matched our real work. We played by the rules even when a mistake helped us. The smaller score（分数） felt more honest（诚实的） than the larger one.

passages.title: The Camera That Stayed in the Bag
paragraphs: My friend wore a funny costume for our play rehearsal. I wanted to take a picture and send it to our class group. Before reaching for my phone, I asked her. She shook her head because her costume was unfinished. I put the phone away. Later, she showed me the finished outfit and asked me to take a photo for her family. We chose one together. A picture of someone is also about their choice（选择）. Asking permission（允许） helped me take care of our friendship as well as the photograph.

passages.title: The Game without a Winner
paragraphs: My brother invented a game in which we had to move ten buttons across a board together. At first, I kept trying to finish my part before him. Then we noticed that one button could not move unless another stayed beside it. We needed to plan as a pair. After several attempts, all ten reached the far side. Neither of us had won alone, but we cheered loudly. The fun came from solving a shared challenge（挑战）. We put the buttons back, ready to have another go with a harder rule（规则）.

passages.title: The Box Labelled Later
paragraphs: I kept unfinished projects in a box labelled “Later”. There was a paper castle, half a bracelet（手链） and a story with no ending. One rainy afternoon, I opened it and chose just one thing. I spent twenty minutes adding an ending to the story. It was short, but it was complete. I did not have to finish everything that day. I only needed to begin somewhere. Before closing the box, I put the bracelet on top. Little by little, a pile of unfinished（未完成的） plans could become something I could enjoy.

passages.title: A Welcome for Next Year
paragraphs: Before moving to a new classroom, we made a guide for the pupils who would use our old one. We explained which cupboard held spare（备用的） pencils and where to put wet umbrellas. I added a note about the window that was difficult to close. Our teacher suggested including something friendly too, so we wrote about our favourite classroom game. I imagined a younger child reading it on a nervous first morning. We were moving on, but a few useful words could help someone else settle in and feel welcome（受欢迎的）.
